relations.note: Achamoth arises indirectly from Sophia’s expelled passion and thus descends from Bythos.
Achamoth retains an odor of immortality left by Christ and the Holy Spirit.
Valentinians consequently call Achamoth Holy Spirit among her cosmological titles.
Theodotean exegesis interprets Jesus as entrusting lower Sophia and her spiritual seed to the Father.
Christ extends through the boundary and gives formless Achamoth substantial existence.
Christ extends through the boundary and gives Achamoth substantial form before withdrawing.
Horos prevents Achamoth from crossing the Pleromatic boundary during her attempted return.

relations.myth: Achamoth’s attempted return to the Pleroma
relations.note: Horos blocks Achamoth from following Christ into the Pleroma and marks her exclusion.
Achamoth enters the Pleroma and becomes the Savior’s bride after the spiritual seed matures.
At consummation Achamoth enters the Pleroma and receives Soter as her spouse.
Seeing the Savior and his angels causes Achamoth to conceive spiritual offspring.
The Savior enlightens Achamoth, separates her passions, and gives her intellectual formation.
Soter separates Achamoth from her passions, gives her form and incorruption’s fragrance, then withdraws.
Autogenes produces the perfect and true Human Adamas.
Autogenes directly emits the true and perfect Human, Adamas.

relations.myth: The perfect Human and Sethian race
relations.note: Adamas appears through the Spirit's foreknowledge and Autogenes's will.

relations.myth: Adamas as the eye of Autogenes
relations.note: Adamas is called Autogenes’s eye, comprehending him as perfect Mind’s word.
Adamas is called Autogenes's eye in the later metaphysical hierarchy.
Autogenes approves Adamas’s manifestation and shares the first aeon with him.
Autogenes mingles with Adamas and joins his praise and petition.

relations.myth: Adamas placed with the first Luminary
relations.note: Adamas resides with the first Luminary in the first aeon.
Adamas is installed with Harmozel in the first aeon.
Adamas is stationed in Harmozel, the first luminary and aeonic dwelling.
The Invisible Spirit wills and names Adamas within the divine aeons.
The Virgin Spirit grants Adamas invincible power.
Heavenly Adamas exists as an image connected with the Spirit and reflected to the lower rulers.
Adamas praises the transcendent Invisible Spirit after receiving his aeonic place.
Rational, psychic, and earthly qualities of the First Man gather in Jesus and speak through him.
Logos mingles with Autogenes and Adamas, then joins their praise and petition.
Adamas is established in the luminous cloud before Nebro and the lower rulers arise.

relations.myth: Norea received into the imperishable realm
relations.note: Norea’s reception is fragmentarily associated with Adamas, called Father of Nous.
The damaged text places Norea in or with primordial Adamas.
Modern functional comparison relates Poimandres to this Sethian heavenly being; no ancient identification exists.
Seth is Adamas’s heavenly son and occupies the second aeon.
Adamas requests Seth from himself so the immovable race may arise.
Adamas produces Seth after an angel’s image and likeness.
Seth praises his father, then father and son jointly praise Barbelo.
Aletheia is Anthropos's higher-order ancestor through her children Logos and Zoe.
Aletheia is emitted with Autogenes as his syzygy.
Bythos and Sige generate Nous and Aletheia within the primordial tetrad.
Bythos and Sigē generate Aletheia together with Nous.
Nous and Aletheia jointly project Christ and Spirit to restore form.
Ekklesia descends from Aletheia through Logos and Zoe.
Truth appears at Barbelo’s request and praises the Spirit and Barbelo.
Aletheia and Nous produce Logos as one member of the next syzygy.
Aletheia is Logos' co-parent with Nous in the principal Ogdoad.
Aletheia is emitted with Nous as his syzygetic partner.
Aletheia is Nous’s female syzygos.

relations.myth: Nous wishes to reveal the Father
relations.note: Aletheia restrains Nous from disclosing the incomprehensible Father to the aeons.
Aletheia forms the second syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Sige receives Bythos's seed and emits Nous together with Aletheia.
Sige produces Aletheia together with Nous as the second syzygy.
Aletheia and Nous produce Zoe together with Logos.
Aletheia and Nous produce Logos and Zoe.
The heavenly Adamas is established beside Autogenes in Harmozel's first aeon.
Anthrōpos descends from Bythos through Nous, Aletheia, Logos, and Zōē.
Some later Valentinians call the Father himself Man, collapsing ancestor and descendant.
The Spirit corresponds to Zoe while the Power of the Highest corresponds to Anthropos.
Anthropos is Ekklesia's syzygetic partner and co-progenitor.
Anthropos and Ekklesia are emanated together by Logos and Zoe.
The heavenly Adamas is assigned to the first aeon within Harmozel's luminary realm.
Hibil Ziwa overcomes dark powers and aids primordial humanity and embodied souls.
The perfect heavenly Human appears or is named with the Invisible Spirit's approval.
First Man confronts Darkness and is overwhelmed after its powers consume his luminous armor.
Living Spirit calls, First Man answers, and Living Spirit draws him from the abyss.
Logos and Zoe emit Anthropos and Ecclesia in the Ptolemaean genealogy.
Colorbasus reverses the standard sequence, making Anthropos and Ecclesia generate Logos and Zoe.
A competing scheme makes Anthropos the immediate source of Logos.
Nous generates the Hermetic Man in his own image and loves him as his child.
Anthropos descends from Nous through Logos and Zoe.
Anthropos forms the fourth syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Poimandres narrates Human's divine origin, cosmic descent, union with Nature, and path to salvation.

relations.myth: Entrapment of Adam in the material cosmos
relations.note: Ruha and her planetary children attempt to tempt, seduce, and entrap Adam.
Seth succeeds Adamas in the next luminary realm and progenates the incorruptible race.
Anthropos descends from Sige through the Nous–Aletheia and Logos–Zoe syzygies.
Logos and Zoe emit Anthropos and Ecclesia in the Ptolemaean genealogy.
Colorbasus reverses the standard sequence, making Anthropos and Ecclesia generate Logos and Zoe.
Anthropos and Zoe arise collectively from the higher Tetrad.
The anointed divine Autogenes is explicitly identified as Christ.
Christ is a distinct superior Light who precedes Autogenes.
The first Luminary appears through Autogenes and governs Adamas's realm.
The four emanate from the light identified as Christ or Autogenes.
Harmozel is the first Luminary attending Autogenes.
The four attend, stand before, and praise Autogenes.
The Spirit generates and anoints Autogenes, who acts according to its will.
Autogenes emerges through the Spirit’s light and Barbelo’s activity.
The Spirit perfects and anoints Autogenes with goodness or divine power.
The Spirit places Autogenes over the divine Fullness.
Logos and Ennoia jointly emit Autogenes.
Later texts describe Autogenes himself as the great or noetic Logos.
Autogenes generates luminous structures above the lower realm where Nebro appears.
Norea cries out to the divine Autogenes and his four holy helpers.
Norea rests in divine Autogenes and, in the usual restoration, generates herself.
Mind is granted to Autogenes as a helper completing the divine Child.
Autogenes becomes or expresses the perfect Mind in later metaphysics.
Modern functional comparison relates these divine intellect figures; no ancient text identifies them.

relations.myth: The perfect Human and Sethian race
relations.note: Seth receives a place in Oroiael's realm beneath Autogenes's higher order.
Seth and Autogenes are blessed together during the visionary ascent.
Seth is placed beneath or generated within the Autogenes order.
Ennoia and Logos jointly emit Autogenes.
Monogenēs, following the Father’s providence, produces Christ to instruct and harmonize the aeons.
Some summaries present Christ as sent more directly by the First Father.
The Father’s providence or command causes the pair’s emission and commissions their restorative work.
Ekklēsia descends from Bythos through Nous, Aletheia, Logos, and Zōē.
The Father, through Monogenēs, produces Horos to stabilize the pleroma and limit Sophia.

relations.myth: Generation of Horos after Sophia’s crisis
relations.note: The Father produces Horos in his image through Monogenes, without a syzygy.
The reconciled aeons present Soter to the Father as their common offering.
Soter reveals the otherwise inaccessible Father and manifests his hidden Name.
Logos descends from Bythos through Nous and Aletheia.
Logos and Zoe jointly emit Bythios as an aeon of the Decad.
The Father opens his mouth and emits Logos as his image.

relations.myth: Nous’s unique knowledge of the Father
relations.note: Bythos grants Nous unique comprehension of the Father.
Nous wishes to disclose Bythos to the aeons, but Sigē checks him.
Bythos and Sigē generate the first-begotten Nous, his image and sole initial comprehender.
Bythos forms the first syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
She is Bythos’s feminine counterpart in the principal Ptolemaean genealogy.
In a variant, Thought is Bythos’s internal disposition rather than a coeternal spouse.
Sigē restrains Nous from prematurely revealing Bythos’s magnitude to the other aeons.
The Father yields sympathetically so that Silence may understand him.
Bythos deposits his projected seed in Sige, who conceives the second syzygy.
The otherwise unyielding Father makes himself yielding so Sige may comprehend him.
Zōē descends from Bythos through Nous and Aletheia.
The spiritual Church is joined to Christ or corporately manifested through his body.

relations.myth: Restoration and instruction of the aeons
relations.note: Ekklesia shares the Pleromatic scene where Christ and Holy Spirit restore order.

relations.myth: Revelation of the true tree of knowledge
relations.note: Christ recounts Epinoia’s work and coordinates his saving revelation with hers.
Christ extends through or beyond Horos/Stauros while giving Achamoth substantial form.

relations.myth: Formation of Achamoth at the Cross-boundary
relations.note: As Stauros, Horos provides the boundary through which Christ extends to form Achamoth.
Christ and Holy Spirit are produced after Horos restores Sophia and then stabilize the aeons.
The pair concurs with the Pleroma in producing Jesus as its collective fruit.
Higher Christ restores the Pleroma; later schemes distinguish him from Soter while connecting their powers.
The Holy Spirit and Christ harmonize the aeons, enabling their collective production of Soter.
Chinese Pure Wind terminology sometimes conflates him with this third-creation deity.

relations.myth: Aeons are instructed after Sophia's disturbance
relations.note: Christ stabilizes and instructs Logos with the other aeons.
Monogenes emits Christ and the Holy Spirit to stabilize the Pleroma.
Nous emits Christ to teach the aeons their origins and the Father’s incomprehensibility.
The Mother Sophia is called the Ogdoad and dwells above the Hebdomad.
Christ and Spirit concur with the united aeons in producing the collective Savior.

relations.myth: Christ enters and unites with the Pleroma
relations.note: Christ leaves Sophia, enters the Pleroma, and unites with the All and Paraclete.

relations.myth: Christ instructs the aeons after Sophia's crisis
relations.note: Christ teaches the aeons about the Father and their own origin.
Holy Spirit teaches the aeons repose, equality, unity, and thanksgiving.
Ruha ḏ-Qudša reuses and polemically devalues the Aramaic designation Holy Spirit.
Christ exposes Saklas's ignorance and descends into his cosmos to awaken humanity.
Logos and Zoe emanate Ekklesia together with Anthropos.
Ekklesia descends from Nous through Logos and Zoe.
Zoe and Logos emanate Ekklesia together with Anthropos.
Eleleth’s Epinoia recognizes the lower order and petitions for another order.
Sethian systems associate a technical Epinoia with the luminary Oroiael.
Norea rests in Epinoia and receives mind and living Logos.
Ennoia of Light hears or receives Norea's invocation.
Norea receives rest in ineffable Epinoia during her restoration.

relations.myth: Saklas seizes the descended Epinoia's power
relations.note: Saklas overpowers Light Epinoia and takes power from her after her descent.
Epinoia manifests in or as spiritual Eve, whom Adam names Life.
The luminous Epinoia is explicitly called Life or Zoe.
All four stand before, praise, and glorify the Invisible Spirit.
Harmozel stands before the Spirit and participates in ordering the aeonic habitations.
Probably following Eleleth’s command, Nebro emerges from the cloud to rule below.
Eleleth descends and drives away the rulers attempting to assault Norea.

relations.myth: Eleleth rescues Norea from the archons
relations.note: Eleleth descends after Norea's cry and terrifies or drives away the rulers.
Scholarship reconstructs Harmozel as one of the four unnamed helpers interceding for Norea.
Eleleth reveals Norea’s imperishable origin and the rulers’ origin and fate.
Eleleth explains the rulers' origin, power, duration, and eventual defeat.
Eleleth narrates Sabaoth’s repentance, praise of Sophia, and heavenly enthronement.
Eleleth’s royal word occasions his appearance, though Sophia remains his prior source.
Sakla appears after Eleleth commands that one rule Chaos and Hades.
Eleleth produces or authorizes Saklas and Nebro within the lower cosmic order.
Eleleth participates with the four luminaries in Seth's celestial commission.
Seth is placed in Oroiael, the second luminary and realm.

relations.myth: Celestial ordering of Adamas and Seth
relations.note: Harmozel houses Adamas within the four-luminary order containing Seth.

relations.myth: Seth stationed in the second aeon
relations.note: Seth is stationed in Oroiael's second celestial aeon.
Modern syncretism compares their revelatory and cosmological functions; no ancient source equates them.
Hibil drains black water, stretches the firmament, and brings living water while Ptahil forms earth.
Priestly material calls Ptahil the son of Hibil and Zahriel.

relations.myth: Removal of Ptahil from the lower region
relations.note: Hibil brings Ptahil out of the lower region during his victorious return.

relations.myth: Ptahil's restoration after the world's end
relations.note: Later tradition expects Hibil to purify or restore Ptahil after material creation ends.
Hibil, acting as Ptahil’s superior helper, completes work Ptahil could not finish.
Hibil penetrates Ruha's realm, outwits or overcomes her, and carries her away.

relations.myth: Hibil impersonates Gaf and promises ascent
relations.note: Hibil disguises himself, claims to lead Ruha to her parents, then confines her.
Despite his deception and violence, Ruha bestows a blessing upon Hibil.
Hibil seals Ruha in an intermediate realm and strikes her when she preaches.
Hibil preserves Ruha and promises later release, though her redemption remains incomplete.
Hibil gives Ruha knowledge concerning her origins, confinement, and eventual liberation.
Hibil tricks Qin, takes Ruha’s mirror, and later removes it from Ur.
Variant supernatural genealogies make Šitil descend through Hibil.

relations.myth: Invocation of the salvific Adamite triad
relations.note: Hibil and Šitil are jointly invoked with Anuš for protection and salvation.
Hibil and Šitil belong to the canonical triad of salvific Adamites.
Horos secures the Pleroma before Soter crosses its boundary to form Achamoth.

relations.myth: Generation of Horos after Sophia’s crisis
relations.note: Monogenes serves as the mediating agency through whom the Father produces Horos.
Horos restrains Sophia while Nous helps articulate and restore Pleromatic order.

relations.myth: Horos establishes the boundary of the Pleroma
relations.note: Horos protects the aeons by separating the Fullness from deficiency.

relations.myth: Hierarchy of the luminous and lower realms
relations.note: Nebro occupies a lower cosmic order beneath the ineffable Spirit.
Modern functional comparison relates these transcendent beings; no ancient text identifies them.
The Spirit is the remote source above Yaldabaoth, not his immediate biological parent.
A voice from the higher realm refutes Yaldabaoth’s claim to be the sole god.
relations.source: Apocryphon of John; Hypostasis of the Archons

relations.note: The Invisible Spirit heads the emanational order from which Seth descends.

relations.myth: Great Seth and the incorruptible race
relations.note: Great Seth serves the Spirit’s divine plan by establishing the incorruptible race and baptism.
relations.source: Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit

relations.myth: Seth petitions the Spirit for his seed
relations.note: Seth praises and petitions the supreme Spirit on behalf of his spiritual race.
Living Silence is associated with the unknown Father as the condition from which triadic powers emerge.
relations.source: Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit

relations.note: All aeons contribute their finest qualities to produce Jesus as their common Fruit.
Jesus receives from Sabaoth a soul-power used in his incarnation.
In Manichaean cosmology Jesus the Splendour emanates from the Third Messenger.
The Living Spirit defeats dark rulers; variants differ on capturing the King.
He counters the King’s attack by rescuing First Man and imprisoning the King’s forces.
He battles Darkness, is overwhelmed, and yields his elemental sons as bait.
Saklas belongs to the demonic order remotely headed by the King of Darkness.
The Messenger’s beauty deceives the King’s host, making archons release seed.
The Messenger deprives Darkness of captured Light, provoking demonic countermeasures.
The Living Spirit awakens him, extends his right hand, and raises him.

relations.myth: Activation of the cosmic purification machine
relations.note: The Messenger activates the cosmos constructed by the Living Spirit.
Different traditions assign the archon-seducing display to one or the other deity.
The Living Spirit helps petition for the further power subsequently emanated as Third Messenger.
Nous emits Logos together with Zoe, with Aletheia as co-parent.
Nous and Aletheia emit Logos.
Logos and Zoe jointly emit this Monogenes as an aeon of the Decad.
Logos forms the third syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.

relations.myth: Logos divides and helps restore the aeons
relations.note: Logos overreaches toward the Father, produces deficient orders, then participates in restoration.

relations.myth: A luminous Logos emerges from divine Mind
relations.note: In the Hermetic account, divine Mind generates a luminous Logos.
Poimandres identifies and explains the luminous Word proceeding from Mind as the divine son.
Sige belongs to the primordial pair ancestral to Logos.
Zoe is Logos' syzygy and co-progenitor of subsequent aeons.
Zoe is Logos’s female syzygy and generative companion.

relations.myth: Variant collective emanation from the higher Tetrad
relations.note: Zoe and Logos arise together with Anthropos and Ecclesia.
Sabaoth repudiates his father; after Sabaoth’s enthronement, Yaldabaoth responds with envy.
Yaldabaoth is Sabaoth’s father and former superior.

relations.myth: Nebro and Saklas organize the lower heavens
relations.note: Nebro and Saklas jointly organize the rulers and administration of the lower heavens.

relations.myth: Nebro creates Saklas as an assistant
relations.note: Nebro creates six angels and Saklas to serve as lower-cosmic assistants.
They emerge separately and each creates six assisting angels.
Seth’s incorruptible generation belongs above, while Nebro rules the lower realm.
Zoe breathes fiery power against Yaldabaoth and casts him down.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.note: Epiphanius reports that the Sethians called Seth's wife Horaia.
Modern scholarship interprets Norea as Seth's female equivalent among paired savior figures.
Norea and Seth are children of Eve.
Nous forms the second syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Nous proceeds from the Father’s maternal Thought.
Nous and Aletheia emit Zoe together with Logos.
Nous and Aletheia produce Logos and Zoe.

relations.myth: Hermetic ascent through seven to eight
relations.note: Poimandres reveals the soul's passage into the Ogdoadic nature.
Sige forms the first syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Zoe forms the third syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Modern syncretism compares their cosmological functions; no ancient source equates them.
Modern typological comparison links their revelatory functions, but no ancient identification is attested.
Ruha collaborates with Ptahil, supplying secrets or lower spirit for material creation.
Ptahil proposes making man in his image and woman in Ruha’s image.
Ruha supplies lower forces and conditions assisting Ptahil’s unstable creation.

relations.myth: Their creative powers rise and fall
relations.note: Ruha’s power increases as Ptahil’s weakens, making their cooperation competitive.
In hostile variants Ruha’s interference damages or corrupts Ptahil’s material world.

relations.myth: Ruha laments to her divine Father
relations.note: Ruha addresses a divine Father, suggesting a possible upper origin left unresolved by the corpus.

relations.myth: Ruha and her powers are subdued
relations.note: The Great Life subdues Ruha and her creatures under Lightworld sovereignty.

relations.myth: Ruha receives the seal of Life
relations.note: Esoteric traditions say Life seals Ruha and her creatures, permitting eventual restoration.
Sabaoth is Yaldabaoth’s son in both repentance narratives.
Yaldabaoth generates Sabaoth as one of his authorities and gives him fire.
Sabaoth is Yaldabaoth’s grandson through Iao in this conflicting genealogy.
Sabaoth recognizes Saklas's error, condemns him, and joins the higher order.
Sabaoth repudiates his father, whose subsequent envy produces Death.
Sabaoth praises Zoe, who helps elevate him and occupies his right side.
Zoe creates seven good androgynous powers in Sabaoth’s presence.
Zoe sits at Sabaoth’s right and teaches him about the eighth heaven.
Pistis gives Zoe authority to teach Sabaoth about the eighth heaven.
relations.source: On the Origin of the World

relations.note: Saklas or the related al-Ṣendīd attacks Seth, whom Adam saves.
Saklas seeks to destroy or enslave heavenly Seth and his incorruptible seed.
relations.source: Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit

relations.note: Seth counters the chief ruler's attempts to destroy his race through saving descents.
relations.source: Apocryphon; Holy Book; Apocalypse of Adam

relations.myth: Saklas copies the Messenger's displayed beauty
relations.note: Saklas and his partner imitate the Third Messenger's male-female form when making humanity.

relations.myth: Creation of humanity after the Messenger's image
relations.note: Ašaqlūn fashions Adam in imitation of the Messenger's displayed form.

relations.myth: Zoe binds Saklas and casts him down
relations.note: Zoe rebukes Saklas; her fiery angel binds him and casts him into Tartarus.
Zoe descends from Sige through Nous and Aletheia.

Abathur.note: Ptahil emanates as Abathur’s image or son at the light-dark boundary.
Abathur.source: Ginza Rabba creation accounts; Diwan Abatur

Abathur.note: Abathur commands Ptahil to create and supplies instructions, material, and hidden mana.
In one strand Abathur punishes Ptahil with a separating bond.
Abathur later restores Ptahil in a variant rehabilitation tradition.

Abatur.note: Hibil stations Abatur at the cosmic boundary to weigh ascending souls.

Abel.note: Mandaean tradition transforms the biblical Abel into Hibil, a pre-existent celestial saviour.
Seth is appointed as replacement offspring after Abel's death.

Abrasax.note: Abrasax ministers to Eleleth, the fourth great light.
Abrasax serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Acinetos.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Acinetos as an aeon of the Decad.

Adam.note: Hidden within Adam, Epinoia awakens him and teaches humanity’s descent and ascent.
The humanized biblical genealogy makes Hibil the son of Adam.

Adam.myth: Pre-existent Hibil approaches Adam and Hawwa
Adam.note: A variant depicts Hibil arriving as a boy before Adam could generate him.
Jesus the Splendour awakens Adam to recognize the divine light imprisoned within him.
The Prince and allied rulers devise Adam as a prison for concentrated Light.
Yaldabaoth and the rulers fashion Adam, then Yaldabaoth animates him with Sophia’s power.
Yaldabaoth restricts and imprisons Adam after humanity surpasses its makers.

Adam.myth: Lower powers attempt to retain Adam
Adam.note: Ruha and the planets seek to confine Adam within the material world.
Ruha mourns because Adam’s death releases the soul-treasure from her control.
Saklas directs Adam's bodily formation, while higher powers provide his spiritual animation.
Saklas orders his angels to make Adam after the likeness and image.

Adam.myth: Demonic partners concentrate light in Adam
Adam.note: Saklas and his partner fashion Adam as an image and prison of divine light.
Earthly Seth is begotten by Adam after the celestial pattern.

Adam.myth: Creation of humanity after the Messenger's image
Adam.note: Adam's body is modeled on the Messenger's radiant heavenly image.
Sophia-Zoe breathes life into Adam’s motionless body.
Adam.source: On the Origin of the World

Adam.note: Epinoia-Zoe indwells Adam and teaches his descent and return.

Adam.myth: Eve and Adam eat from knowledge
Adam.note: Zoe’s instructive complex enables Adam to eat and gain knowledge.
Adam.source: On the Origin of the World

Adam Kasia.myth: The hidden Adam enters Adam Pagria
Adam Kasia.note: The transcendent soul or archetypal Adam is placed within Ptahil’s material Adam.

Adam Pagria.note: Ptahil forms Adam’s body in his image, clothes it, and tries to animate it.

Adamas of Light.note: He is the Living Spirit’s warrior son.
Armed with sword and shield, Adamas restrains the powers of Darkness.

Adonai.note: Polemical passages describe Ruha as Adonai’s mistress or lover.
Ruha and Adonai are associated as political-religious allies of Jerusalem’s lower order.
Sabaoth is repeatedly invoked beside Adonai in magical formulas.

Adonaios.note: One list names the fifth authority Adonaiou, called Sabaoth.

Aerosiel.note: Aerosiel serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Agape.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Agape with Metrikos.

Agathos Daimon.note: Modern scholarship proposes identification through structural comparison with other Hermetic teachers.

Ageratos.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Ageratos as an aeon of the Decad.

Ainos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Ainos with Synesis.

All aeons of the Pleroma.myth: The common Fruit of the Pleroma
All aeons of the Pleroma.note: All aeons contribute their finest qualities and jointly produce Soter as their common offering.

Allogenes.note: Allogenes approaches the Spirit through mediated instruction, abstraction, and unknowing rather than direct conversation.

Answer.note: The Answer rises from First Man against the surrounding Darkness.
The Answer rises responsively from the First Man toward the Living Spirit.

Anuš.note: Hibil and Anuš appear as members of the three salvific Adamites.
A variant genealogy makes Anuš descend from Šitil and ultimately from Hibil.

Anuš.myth: Invocation of the salvific Adamite triad
Anuš.note: Hibil and Anuš are jointly invoked with Šitil for protection and salvation.
Related Mandaean narratives present Anuš as the heavenly messenger who exposes Jesus.

Anuš Uthra.note: Anuš repeatedly frustrates Ruha’s building and ultimately destroys Jerusalem despite her pleas.

Anuš Uthra.myth: Ruha offers to destroy Jerusalem’s inhabitants
Anuš Uthra.note: Ruha offers to kill the hostile inhabitants for Anuš, but he refuses.

Anōš.myth: Three heavenly Adamites aid the Light
Anōš.note: Anōš and Šitil jointly serve as heavenly Adamite helpers.

Aphtharsia.note: Aphtharsia and Christ emit the four Luminaries surrounding Autogenes.

Archon of the Hebdomad.note: He governs the Hebdomad beneath the Great Archon's Ogdoad.

Arrhetos.note: In the system attributed to Valentinus, Sige and Arrhetos form the initial Dyad.

Astaphaios.note: Astaphaios is one of Yaldabaoth’s three principal sons.
Astaphaios.source: On the Origin of the World

Attis.myth: Naassene interpretation of the Attis hymn
Attis.note: Naassene exegesis interprets the Phrygian Attis through its doctrine of the primal Man.

Authades.note: Jesus counters Self-Willed and the emanations sent to oppress Pistis Sophia.

Autophyes.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Autophyes as an aeon of the Decad.

Ayar.note: Ayar breathes upon Ptahil’s solid work and dries the earth with his wings.

Behron.note: Behron serves as a carpenter within Ptahil’s collaborative creation complex.

Bihram.note: Bihram and Hibil are invoked together as salvific powers in baptismal liturgy.

Cain.note: Seth replaces Cain's murdered brother and founds the alternative protected lineage.

Call.note: The Call descends to rescue First Man from the King’s Darkness.
The Living Spirit emanates or clothes himself in the personified downward Call.
Some accounts count the personified Call as the Living Spirit’s sixth son.

Church.myth: Logos separates from and returns toward the Totality
Church.note: Logos acts individually within the Totality; his separated members require reintegration.

Column of Glory.note: One canonical scheme makes the Messenger produce the ascending celestial route.
A competing scheme lists the Column beside the Messenger as coordinate powers.

Daveithe.note: Scholarship reconstructs Daveithe as one of the four unnamed helpers interceding for Norea.
Daveithe's third aeon becomes the station of Seth's spiritual seed.

Death.note: Death occupies the sixth heaven vacated when Sabaoth was elevated.
Zoe produces seven good powers against Death’s seven androgynous offspring.
Death.source: On the Origin of the World

Demiurgic Christ.myth: Composite incarnation of the earthly Savior
Demiurgic Christ.note: Achamoth supplies the spiritual first fruits joined with the psychic Christ supplied by the Demiurge.

Demiurgic Mind.myth: The Hermetic Man encounters the cosmos
Demiurgic Mind.note: Demiurgic rational activity orders the cosmos through which the Hermetic Man passes.

Dinanukht.myth: Ruha reveals herself as cosmic opposites
Dinanukht.note: As Ewat, Ruha proclaims to Dinanukht her union of light, darkness, truth, error, life, and death.
Ruha appears as the female ruler and seductress of Dinanukht’s third astral station.

Divine Powers of the Ogdoad.note: After completing his instruction, Poimandres mingles with or enters the powers.

Earthly Jesus.note: Soter descends upon Jesus as a dove, bringing the powers of the Pleroma.
In one scheme the impassible Soter withdraws before Pilate, leaving the lower Jesus to suffer.

Ecclesia.note: Aletheia is Ecclesia's higher-order ancestor through her children Logos and Zoe.
Ecclesia is Anthropos' female syzygos and co-generator of twelve aeons.
Restored female aeons assimilate to Spirit and Ecclesia, making Spirit a model for the church.
Logos and Zoe emit Ecclesia together with Anthropos.
Ecclesia forms the fourth syzygy and is a member of the primary Ogdoad.
Ecclesia descends from Sige through the Nous–Aletheia and Logos–Zoe syzygies.
Logos and Zoe jointly emit Ecclesia.
Ecclesia and Zoe arise collectively from the higher Tetrad.

Ekklesiastikos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Ekklesiastikos with Makariotes.

Elainos.note: Elainos serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Eloai.note: Eloai is one of Yaldabaoth’s three principal sons.
Eloai.source: On the Origin of the World

Elohim.note: One recension names Elohim as Yaldabaoth’s son by Eve.

Elpis.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Elpis with Patrikos.

Enoš.note: Enoš joins the cosmic bow or firmament during Ptahil’s earth-making operation.

Error.note: Error persecutes Jesus, but his revelation dissolves Error and the ignorance sustaining it.

Error.myth: Error persecutes the revealer and knowledge dissolves Error
Error.note: Error persecutes the revelatory Logos and is dissolved when he reveals the Father.

Eternal Life.note: Eternal Life appears at Barbelo’s request and praises the Spirit and Barbelo.

Eve.note: Dark anthropogony fashions Eve so reproduction keeps Light divided and embodied.
Yaldabaoth sexually violates or defiles Eve; the text does not make her his consort.
Eve bears Norea after bearing Seth.
Saklas commands the creation of Eve alongside Adam.

Eve.myth: Demonic partners concentrate light in Eve
Eve.note: Saklas and his partner fashion Eve as an image and prison of divine light.
Some comparatively late Manichaean reports portray Saklas or his counterpart seducing Eve.
Eve bears earthly Seth through God as Abel's replacement.

Eve.myth: Creation of humanity after the Messenger's image
Eve.note: Her sexual differentiation continues the demonic imitation of his polyvalent image.
Zoe appears as or through spiritual Eve, distinct from her fleshly likeness.
The text names Eve-Zoe as the virginal female instructor of life.
Eve.source: On the Origin of the World

Father.note: The pre-existent Church proceeds as the innumerable issue of Father and Son.

Father.myth: Logos attempts to comprehend the Father
Father.note: Logos reaches toward the incomprehensible Father without proper mediation, precipitating division.
Those entering the Ogdoad hymn the Father, and its powers ascend toward him.

Father of All.note: Norea cries to the supreme God for rescue and is received into the celestial order.

Father of Greatness.myth: Emanation and commissioning of First Man
Father of Greatness.note: The Father ultimately calls forth First Man as his champion against Darkness.
The King’s invasion opposes the Father, who evokes defenders of Light.
The Father commissions and ultimately brings forth the Living Spirit’s emanational sequence.
Modern typological comparison links these supreme divine figures, but no ancient identification is attested.
The Primal Man is the Father’s son, emanation, or self-manifestation.
The Father commissions and sends him to defend Light against Darkness.
The Father calls forth the Third Messenger to recover Light.

Father of Nous.note: Norea is given repose or placement in the Father of Nous.

Father–Mother–Son triad.note: The triadic powers come forth from living Silence and praise the Great Invisible Spirit.
Father–Mother–Son triad.source: Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit

First Life.myth: Commission for the descent into Darkness
First Life.note: First Life authorizes, empowers, and ultimately receives Hibil after his mission.

First Man.note: First Man confronts the dark powers and sacrifices his light-elements.
The Living Spirit calls, extends his right hand, and raises him from Darkness.
They ascend with the Mother of Life and petition the Father.

First Man.myth: Recovery of the First Man's light-elements
First Man.note: The Messenger helps recover his lost light-elements and answers his appeal.

First Mystery.note: Jesus acts at the First Mystery’s command and as its extension or manifestation.

Five Sons.note: First Man wears his Five Sons as armor and offers them in battle.

Five sons of the Living Spirit.note: They descend with the Living Spirit, locate him, and subdue demons.

Foreknowledge.note: Adamas emerges from Foreknowledge and perfect Mind through divine will.
Foreknowledge appears at Barbelo’s request and praises the Spirit and Barbelo.

Friend of the Lights.note: The Friend evokes the Great Builder, beginning the Living Spirit’s emanational lineage.

Gaf.note: Gaf is Ruha’s brother in the darkness-family genealogy.
Gaf is Ruha’s intended husband and impregnates her with Ur.

Gamaliel.note: Gamaliel ministers to Harmozel, the first great light.
Gamaliel serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Great Architect.note: The Messenger commands him to build Paradise and imprison Light's enemies.

Great Archon.note: The Ogdoad is the cosmic jurisdiction ruled by the Great Archon.

Great Archon's Son.note: The wiser Son enlightens the Great Archon within the Ogdoadic administration.

Great Builder.note: The Great Builder directly calls forth the Living Spirit.

Great Nous.note: Modern typological comparison links these intellect figures, but no ancient identification is attested.

Hawa.note: Ptahil forms Hawa after Adam’s image in one version.

Hawa.myth: Creation of Hawa in Ruha’s image
Hawa.note: Another passage has Ptahil form Hawa after Ruha’s image and join her animation.
Ptahil proposes Adam as his image and Hawa as Ruha’s image.
Ruha induces Hawa to lament Adam noisily, opposing Mandaean mortuary ideals.
Ruha expresses attachment and deprivation when Hibil removes Hawa.

Hawwa.note: Hibil is called Hawwa's son despite accounts in which he pre-exists procreation.

Hawwa.myth: Pre-existent Hibil approaches Adam and Hawwa
Hawwa.note: Hibil arrives before ordinary procreation while still being designated Hawwa's son.

Hayyi Rabbi.note: Ptahil is the Fourth Life within the emanation chain originating in Great Life.
Great Life ultimately commissions or permits Ptahil’s material creation indirectly.
Great Life eventually accepts or restores Ptahil in rehabilitation passages.

Hedone.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Hedone as an aeon of the Decad.

Helen of Troy.note: Ennoia is said to inhabit Helen, whose abduction causes the Trojan War.

Henosis.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Henosis as an aeon of the Decad.

Hermes Trismegistus.note: Poimandres grants Hermes a cosmic vision, explains salvation, and commissions him to guide humanity.
Modern harmonization identifies them nonliterally, despite their distinct teacher-pupil roles in the ancient dialogue.

Hibil.myth: Three heavenly Adamites aid the Light
Hibil.note: Hibil and Šitil jointly serve as heavenly Adamite helpers.

Higher Savior.note: Sabaoth models his Jesus Christ upon the Savior in the eighth heaven.

Hylē.note: One tradition makes female Matter the generative source of dark rulers.
Kephalaia 6 merges or transfers Hylē’s attributes into the male King.

Iao.note: Iao generates Sabaoth in a descending genealogy of rulers.
Sabaoth is repeatedly invoked beside Iao as a powerful divine name.

Imperishable Ones.note: After restoration, Norea joins the imperishable beings of the higher realm.

Incorruptibility.note: Incorruptibility participates with Christ and light in producing the four.
Incorruptibility appears at Barbelo’s request and praises the Spirit and Barbelo.

Israel.note: Sabaoth creates Israel as his firstborn heavenly being.

Ištar.note: A compound Ginza name associates Ruha with the Venus–Ishtar complex.

Jabraoth.note: Sabaoth and Jabraoth occur in divisions of repentant and hostile powers.

Jehovah.note: Blavatsky equates Jehovah with Ialdabaoth in her universal esoteric synthesis.

Jesus.note: Some Valentinians derive Jesus from Anthropos and Ecclesia; rival schools give other origins.
Some reported Valentinians derive Jesus from Ekklesia and Anthropos.
Jesus summons Eleleth, Daueithel, and Harmosiel, who introduce themselves as angels.
As Cross and Limit, Horos enables Jesus to carry the Seed into the Pleroma.
Jesus’s sayings reveal Horos’s sustaining and separating powers.
Logos joins all aeons in contributing excellence to produce the common fruit Jesus.
Jesus exposes Nebro’s subordinate cosmic status without personally encountering him.
Nous joins all the aeons in producing the composite Savior.
Jesus brings the Gospel through the Ogdoad and distinguishes confused cosmic levels.
Jesus' numerical value 888 expresses Ogdoadic and decadic structures.
Anti-Christian polemics call Jesus the son of Ruha ḏ-Qudša.
Jesus enters Sabaoth the Good and embraces the light-power within him.

Jesus.myth: Jesus exposes sacrifice offered to Saklas
Jesus.note: Jesus identifies the disciples' corrupted worship and sacrifices as service to Saklas.
Seth prepares a body and assumes Jesus in a functional incarnation.
Through Jesus, Seth defeats and nails the archontic powers.

Jesus Christ.note: Sabaoth creates a Christ modeled on the higher Savior.
Sabaoth and his Christ jointly receive the manifestation of embodied souls.

Jesus the Splendour.note: Jesus awakens Adam and opposes the dark rulers’ imprisoning design.
Modern typological comparison links their saving revelation, but no ancient identification is attested.
Jesus proceeds within or from the Messenger's divine evocation.
Jesus continues the Messenger's salvific work by awakening Adam.

Jeu.note: The Great Sabaoth occupies a rank beneath Jeu in the heavenly hierarchy.

Judas.note: DeConick reconstructs Judas as aligned with Nebro, but the text narrates no meeting.

Judas.myth: Judas sacrifices the body clothing Jesus
Judas.note: Judas's disputed sacrifice of Jesus's mortal body is associated with sacrifice to Saklas.

Kalyptos.note: Kalyptos is the hidden mode perceived above Autogenes.

Keeper of Splendor.note: He is the Living Spirit’s son, generated during the second creation.
The Keeper sustains the ten heavens within the Living Spirit’s cosmic structure.

King of Glory.note: He is the Living Spirit’s son, generated during the second creation.
The King manages celestial rotation or the heavenly structures.

King of Honor.note: He is the Living Spirit’s son, generated during the second creation.
The King governs cosmic structures and assists the recovery of Light.

Kingdom.myth: Sevenfold imitation of the higher realm
Kingdom.note: Sabaoth is paired with the higher power Kingdom.

Kronos.myth: Invocation of the three great ones
Kronos.note: A gem depicting Kronos invokes Sabaoth with Iao and Adonai.

Krun.note: Hibil overpowers, binds, and seals Krun, neutralizing his power.
Hibil obtains Krun's secret name or the governing power of Darkness.

Light.note: Light is one of his five elemental sons.
He arms himself with Light as armor or weapon before its dispersal.

Light Form.note: The Light Form belongs to the rescue hierarchy descending from his evocation.

Light dwelling in the heights.note: Norea addresses the transcendent Light dwelling in the heights.

Light-Nous.note: The Light-Mind counters the King’s continuing power within embodied humanity.

Light-Nous.myth: Emanational hierarchy of the Third Evocation
Light-Nous.note: The Light-Nous follows Jesus downstream from the Messenger's evocation.

Living Air.note: Living Air is one of his five elemental sons.
He puts Living Air on as armor before its capture by Darkness.

Living Fire.note: Living Fire is one of his five elemental sons.
He wears Fire as his first robe or principal weapon.

Living Water.note: Living Water is one of his five elemental sons.
He puts Water on as armor before it becomes captive Living Soul.

Macaria.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Macaria as an aeon of the Decad.

Maiden of Light.note: She displays herself to male archons, causing release of swallowed Light.

Makariotes.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Makariotes with Ekklesiastikos.

Manda d-Hayyi.note: One emanational genealogy says Manda d-Hayyi creates Hibil Ziwa.

Manda d-Hayyi.myth: Commission for the descent into Darkness
Manda d-Hayyi.note: Manda d-Hayyi sends Hibil on his mission into the lower worlds.
Manda d-Hayyi sends a messenger-letter or bird to aid Hibil's return.
Some passages substitute Manda d-Hayyi for Hibil or merge their actions.
Modern syncretism compares their revelatory and light-world functions; no ancient source equates them.
One creation tract presents Ptahil as the son of Manda d-Hayyi.
Manda d-Hayyi secretly inserts and protects Adam’s soul beyond Ptahil’s control.

Manda d-Hiia.note: The Gnosis of Life participates in the light-world mission that instructs Adam.
Mandaean tradition sends this heavenly messenger to expose Jesus as a false or deceptive messiah.
Manda d-Hiia possibly rescues Ruha through the inferred identification of her with Nitufta.

Melchizedek.note: Jesus explains Melchizedek’s cosmic role in purification and transporting light.

Metrikos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Metrikos with Agape.

Michar.note: Michar serves as a baptismal minister or protector of Seth's race.

Micheus.note: Micheus serves as a baptismal minister or protector of Seth's race.

Mirothea.note: Mirothea is explicitly called the mother of Pigeradamas.
Mirothea is associated with Adamas and Autogenes's manifestation.

Mirothoe.note: Mirothoe gives birth to Adamas as light radiating from light.

Mixis.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Mixis as an aeon of the Decad.

Mnesinous.note: Mnesinous serves as a baptismal minister or protector of Seth's race.

Mother of Life.myth: Emanation and commissioning of First Man
Mother of Life.note: The Mother of Life produces or calls forth First Man for battle.
The Father evokes her in response to the King’s invasion.
She accompanies or assists the Living Spirit during the First Man’s rescue.
They construct the universe from the defeated demons’ bodies and skins.
They ascend with the First Man and petition the Father for another power.
She evokes, emanates, or bears the Primal Man.
He prays to his Mother, who appeals upward for his rescue.
Her appeal with other light-powers prompts the Messenger's salvific deployment.
Mother of Life.source: Theodore bar Kōnay, Book of Scholia XI

Mother-Father.note: The higher merciful power sends Epinoia to help Adam and restore creation.

Māra.note: Central Asian texts identify the adversarial office using a Buddhist demon-name.

Naamah.note: Pearson equates Norea with Naamah through name meanings and later primordial traditions.

Nahashbat.note: This victory-crown-bearing angel precedes him into battle in eastern summaries.

Nairyō.saŋha.note: Iranian communities identify him with the Zoroastrian divine herald.

Namrāʾēl.note: She mates with Ašaqlūn in the demonic response to his displayed image.

Nature.myth: The Hermetic Man's union with Nature
Nature.note: The Man and Nature love one another and unite, producing terrestrial humanity's double nature.
Poimandres interprets Nature's love, embrace, and union with Human, which produces seven androgynous humans.

Nbaṭ-Rba.note: Hibil addresses Nbaṭ as his father in the priestly dialogue.
Nbaṭ answers Hibil's questions and supplies esoteric priestly mysteries.

Nebroel.note: Nebroel and her regional equivalents are Saklas's female procreative partner.

Nebroel.myth: Demonic partners fashion Adam and Eve
Nebroel.note: Together they consume light-bearing offspring, copulate, and fashion the first human couple.
Nebroel.source: Coptic, Iranian, and Syriac Manichaean texts

Nebruel.note: Nebruel emerges with Sakla after Eleleth’s command in a damaged passage.

Nidbai.note: Nidbai is invoked with Hibil and other light-beings in baptismal prayer.

Nitufta.note: Buckley reconstructs Nitufta as Ruha’s redeemed form, though the text never explicitly equates them.

Noah.note: Epiphanius's Noria tradition presents her as Noah's wife.
Noah refuses Norea admission, and she destroys or burns his ark.

Parakletos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Parakletos with Pistis.

Pater.note: In the variant attributed to Valentinus, Aletheia forms the second dyad with Pater.
In Valentinus's reported variant, Pater proceeds from the Arrhetos–Sige Dyad.
Pater directly produces Zoe and three other aeons in Valentinus’s variant.

Patrikos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Patrikos with Elpis.

Perfect Knowledge.note: Perfect Knowledge is emitted with and joined to Adamas.
Through Perfect Knowledge, Adamas knows the transcendent source.

Pistis.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Pistis with Parakletos.
A heavenly voice associated with Pistis exposes Yaldabaoth’s false claim to sole divinity.
Pistis.source: On the Origin of the World

Pistis Sophia.note: Jesus sends light-power, defeats her oppressors, crowns her, and restores her to the thirteenth aeon.
The lion-faced power associated with Yaldabaoth consumes or strips light from Pistis Sophia.
Zoe is explicitly called the daughter of Pistis Sophia.
Pistis gives her daughter Zoe authority to instruct Sabaoth.
Pistis Sophia.source: On the Origin of the World

Plesithea.note: Plesithea comes forth through Seth and bears or supplies his seed.

Pronoia.myth: Providence descends into the lower cosmos
Pronoia.note: Providence counters Yaldabaoth by awakening and liberating the human seed from his power.

Pronoia.myth: Pronoia tricks Saklas into empowering Adam
Pronoia.note: Pronoia secretly causes Saklas to transfer Sophia's stolen power into Adam.
Providence sends rescuers who remove Zoe before the ruler assaults Eve’s likeness.

Prophania.note: Prophania is a maternal manifestation associated with the Lights beneath Autogenes.

Protennoia.note: Protennoia calls herself the life of her Epinoia dwelling within cosmic beings.

Protennoia.myth: Protennoia manifests as Logos in her third descent
Protennoia.note: Logos is Protennoia's third revelatory manifestation, not an independent offspring.

Protophanes-Harmedon.note: Protophanes-Harmedon is the noetic first-appearing mode above Autogenes.

Prunicus.note: Prunicus providentially generates Seth in Irenaeus's hostile account.

Psychic Christ.note: Soter descends upon the psychic Christ or prepared Jesus as his lower vehicle.

Pyrrha.note: Epiphanius connects Noria with fiery Pyrrha through the ark-burning story and a fire etymology.

Qin.note: Hibil induces Qin to disclose the secret mysteries guarded in her world.

Qin.myth: Taking Qin's jewel, mirror, and herb
Qin.note: Hibil secretly takes or masters Qin's pearl, mirror, and bitter herb.
Qin is Ruha’s mother in the darkness-family genealogy.
Esoteric texts sometimes collapse Qin and Ruha into one darkness-power.

Samblo.note: Samblo ministers to Daveithai, the third great light.
Samblo serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Savior.myth: The Church becomes the Savior's body
Savior.note: The Church or spiritual seed is interpreted as the Savior's flesh or body.

Savior.myth: The Savior completes Logos' restorative economy
Savior.note: The Savior completes what Logos cannot and gathers the spiritual members toward restoration.
One faction derives the Savior specifically from the ten descendants of Logos and Zoe.

Saviour.note: Bythos and the harmonized aeons jointly contribute their best qualities to produce the Saviour.
The Saviour manifests and reveals the unknown Father outside the pleroma.

Seldao.note: Seldao serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Selmechel.note: Selmechel serves as an angelic protector assigned to Seth's race.

Seth’s incorruptible seed.note: Seth’s seed and saintly souls dwell or repose in Daveithai.

Seven Governors.myth: Formation and rule of the governors
Seven Governors.note: Poimandres reveals their formation, circular government, powers, and role in fate.

Shehlon.note: Shehlon insults Ptahil, opposes creation, and predicts Life will reject his offering.

Shehrun.note: Shehrun serves as a carpenter within Ptahil’s collaborative creation complex.

Shem.note: Some Mandaean passages or interpretations make Nuraita the wife of Shem.

Simat Hiia.note: Some liturgical traditions identify Ruha with Simat Hiia or treat her as Ruha’s redeemed counterpart.

Simon.note: Simon generates Ennoia as his First Thought or First Conception.
Simon descends through the cosmic powers to recover the imprisoned Ennoia.

Son.note: The pre-existent Church proceeds as the innumerable issue of Father and Son.

Son.myth: The Son reveals himself to converted Logos
Son.note: The Son gives Logos knowledge, stability, and the pattern for restoration.

Sophia’s Enthymesis.note: Horos separates, fences off, and expels the shapeless product from the Pleroma.
Tertullian says Horos crucifies the Enthymesis and Passion outside the Pleroma.

Soter’s angels.myth: Generation of Soter and his retinue
Soter’s angels.note: The angels are produced alongside Soter as counterparts of the future spiritual seed.

Souriel.note: Souriel is jointly invoked with Daveithe or Eleleth in Christian spells.

Spiritual Church.note: The pneumatic Church or spiritual seed derives from Achamoth and matures through gnosis.

Spiritual Seed.myth: Crossing the Limit into the Pleroma
Spiritual Seed.note: The Cross marks and carries the Seed, whose qualified members may pass the Limit.

Srōš.note: Mandaean systematization equates Šitil with the Iranian being Srōš.

Syncrasis.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit Syncrasis as an aeon of the Decad.

Synesis.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Synesis with Ainos.

The Answer.note: The Primal Man responds through the personified Answer, initiating his ascent.

The Call.note: The personified Call reaches and awakens the unconscious Primal Man.

The Church.myth: Assumption and ascent of the Church
The Church.note: Jesus Christ receives the spiritual and psychic Church and bears them upward.

The Tetrad.myth: Marcus and the body of Truth
The Tetrad.note: The female Tetrad reveals mysteries, while Aletheia separately manifests as an alphabetic body.

The Twelve zodiacal powers.note: The Twelve assist or condition Ptahil’s formation of the material cosmos and bodies.

The Twelve zodiacal signs.note: Ruha and Ur are parents of the Twelve zodiacal beings.
The Twelve participate under Ruha’s sovereignty in fate and obstruction of souls.
The Twelve zodiacal signs.source: Ginza Rabba; Book of the Zodiac

The children of Ptahil.note: Magical texts describe destructive ruin-guardians collectively as Ptahil’s children or creations.
Ptahil’s creations damage human dwellings and are bound or expelled by protective magic.

Theletos.note: Ekklesia and Anthropos generate Theletos with Sophia.
Horos restores Sophia to conjunction with her consort Theletos.

Thelēsis.note: In a variant, Will supplies effective generative force alongside Thought.

Tree.note: A Tree called Gnosis proceeds from Adamas and Perfect Knowledge.

Triple-Male Child.note: The Triple-Male Child is closely coordinated or partially identified with Autogenes.

Triple-Powered One.note: The Triple-Powered One is variously the Spirit’s potency, immediate hypostasis, or the Spirit itself.

Twelve Virgins of Light.note: The Messenger brings forth the twelve female powers in Theodore's hierarchy.
Twelve Virgins of Light.source: Theodore bar Kōnay, Book of Scholia XI

Twelve Virgins of Light.note: The Virgins display luminous beauty before archons at the Messenger's direction.

Upper Sophia.note: Achamoth is Upper Sophia’s expelled Enthymesis, defective product, or daughter.

Ur.note: Hibil neutralizes the dark king Ur and removes Ruha from his realm.

Ur.myth: Creation from the realm of darkness
Ur.note: Ptahil’s creation uses matter implicated in Ur’s dark realm, without preserved direct dialogue.
Ruha bears the dragon Ur after becoming pregnant by Gaf.
Ruha sleeps with her son Ur and generates the planetary powers.

Ur.myth: Ruha and Ur generate astral rulers
Ur.note: Ruha and Ur jointly produce powers governing fate and the lower cosmos.

Ur.myth: Ruha opposes Ur’s attack on Light
Ur.note: Ur wants war against the Light, but Ruha counsels attacking darkness instead.

Virgin of Light.note: One canonical arrangement places the Virgin among powers produced by the Messenger.
She displays beautiful forms as his principal agent or variant counterpart.
Virgin of Light.source: Ephrem; Coptic, Syriac, and Iranian traditions

Voice of Truth.note: Norea addresses the Voice, which participates in her reception into the higher realm.

Wind.note: Wind is one of his five elemental sons.
He puts Wind on as living armor before it enters the Mixture.

Yahweh.note: One recension names Yahweh as Yaldabaoth’s son by Eve.
Modern harmonizations identify Saklas directly with Yahweh beyond the texts' qualified creator polemic.

Yao.note: Yao is one of Yaldabaoth’s three principal sons.
Yao.source: On the Origin of the World

Yawar Ziwa.note: Prayer 80 invokes Yawar Ziwa and Hibil separately among salvific powers.
Identification with Simat Hiia indirectly places Ruha as Yawar Ziwa’s bride.

Yesseus Mazareus Yessedekeus.note: Yesseus Mazareus Yessedekeus ministers baptism and protection to Seth's race.

Yew.note: Jesus invokes and teaches mysteries associated with Yew, whom he calls father of his father.

Yoel.note: Yoel holds a fifth-light or baptismal presidency without replacing the tetrad.

Youel.note: Youel mediates knowledge of the Triple-Powered One and unknowable Spirit to Allogenes.

Yukašar.note: The Book of John identifies Yukašar as Ptahil’s son.

Yusmir.note: Yusmir serves as a carpenter within Ptahil’s collaborative creation complex.

Yōšamin.note: Yōšamin precedes Ptahil in the canonical chain of emanated Lives.
Ptahil says Yōšamin initiated the great conflict at the cosmic boundary.

Yōšamin.myth: Collaborative creation of the lower world
Yōšamin.note: The creators bring Yōšamin and request his children as lower-world lights.

Zahreil.note: Ptahil is called Zahreil’s son in mythic and liturgical genealogies.

Zahriel.note: Hibil and Zahriel are named together as Ptahil's parents.
Zahriel is named as Ruha’s sister.

Zostrianos.note: Zostrianos ascends through baptisms and revelations toward the Triple-Powered Invisible Spirit.

all aeons.note: Christ teaches the aeons proper conjunction and the Father’s incomprehensibility.
Holy Spirit teaches thanksgiving, equalizes the aeons, and leads them to repose.

angel of wrath.note: Sophia stations the angel at Sabaoth’s left, which typifies injustice.

angels and archangels.note: Ennoia produces the angels and powers that subsequently form the visible world.

angels and powers.note: Her jealous offspring imprison Ennoia and subject her to repeated humiliation.

creative Mind.myth: Logos joins creative Mind to order the cosmos
creative Mind.note: The Hermetic Logos joins the creative Mind in separating and ordering the elements.

earthly Adam.note: Earthly Adam is fashioned by lower rulers in the likeness of Adamas.

female archons.note: His luminous youths arouse them into discharging Light or miscarrying.

fiery angel.note: Zoe breathes forth a fiery angel to bind and cast down Yaldabaoth.

fiery angel of Zoe.note: Witnessing the angel defeat and bind Yaldabaoth prompts Sabaoth’s repentance.

five Sons of the First Man.note: The King’s matching dark powers swallow or bind the five sons.
five Sons of the First Man.source: Acta Archelai; Coptic and Iranian texts

four holy helpers.note: Four unnamed holy helpers intercede for Norea before the Father.

living Logos.note: Norea invokes the untouchable Logos and later inherits the living Logos.

male archons.note: His luminous female forms arouse them into releasing seed containing Light.

perfect Mind.note: Adamas emerges from perfect Mind and Foreknowledge through divine will.

seven archangels of Sophia.note: The seven archangels remove Sabaoth from the heavenly war.
After rescuing Sabaoth, the seven archangels stand before him as servants.

seven good androgynous powers.note: Zoe produces seven beneficent powers as counterparts to Death’s progeny.
seven good androgynous powers.source: On the Origin of the World

souls destined for bodies.note: The souls are manifested to Sabaoth and his Christ before embodiment.

souls of Seth’s offspring.note: The souls of Seth’s offspring repose in Eleleth.

souls of dead children.myth: Baptism and release of dead children
souls of dead children.note: Hibil baptizes deceased children's souls so they may continue toward the World of Light.

the Decad.note: Logos and Zoe jointly emit ten further aeons.

the Savior’s angels.note: Achamoth generates spiritual offspring patterned after the angels she sees with the Savior.
Her perfected spiritual offspring become brides of the Savior’s angels at restoration.

the aeons.note: The pleromatic aeons ultimately unfold from Bythos’s hidden generative abundance.
Once harmonized, the aeons glorify the Father and contribute their best qualities.
Horos preserves the aeons’ ordered Fullness by limiting extension and excluding deficiency.
Nous seeks their enlightenment; his emissions spread knowledge, equality, praise, and concord among them.

the descending Dove.note: Valentinians identify the descending dove with the Spirit of the Father’s Thought.

the disciple.note: The disciple enters the Eighth through prayer and undergoes visionary transformation.
the disciple.source: Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth

the psychic Christ.note: A Pleromatic Savior or spiritual power descends upon the psychic Christ, with competing accounts of their union.

the seed of Seth.note: Seth is father and archetype of the incorruptible spiritual race.
Seth descends during flood, conflagration, and judgment to save his race.

the serpent.note: Epinoia supplies true understanding, contrasting with the serpent’s corrupt instruction.
The spiritual female works through the serpent to teach Eve and Adam.
Eve-Zoe is the higher instructor figure while the wise Beast instructs Eve.
the serpent.source: On the Origin of the World

the seven Governors.myth: The Hermetic Man traverses the spheres
the seven Governors.note: The Man traverses their spheres and shares in their nature, powers, and rule.

the six angels of Nebro.note: Nebro creates six angels as his attendants.
Nebro’s six attendants help produce the twelve heavenly angels.

the subordinate archons.note: Yaldabaoth generates twelve authorities and distributes portions of his fire to them.
The subordinate rulers serve under Yaldabaoth’s command.

the twelve angels.note: Nebro’s and Saklas’s assistants generate or establish twelve heavenly angels.
The twelve angels each receive an individual heavenly portion.

the twelve-aeon Dodecad.note: Anthropos and Ecclesia jointly emit the twelve aeons completing the Thirty.

the younger Adam.myth: Ruha impersonates the younger Adam’s wife
the younger Adam.note: Disguised as his wife, Ruha seduces the younger Adam.
Ruha reveals that division into male and female arose from cosmic imbalance.

three soul-guiding angels.note: Three angels belong to the soul-guiding hierarchy descending from his evocation.

twelve lower angels.myth: Angels appointed over Chaos and Hades
twelve lower angels.note: A conjecturally restored Eleleth calls twelve angels into being to rule below.

upright Nous.note: Norea appeals to Nous and inherits Mind in her restored state.

Āz.note: Iranian traditions variously treat Āz as the King’s identity or counterpart.
Some Iranian formulations subordinate Āz as the binding appetite serving Darkness.

Āz.myth: Āz devises humanity as a light-prison
Āz.note: Saklas and his partner function as embodiments, garments, or instruments of Āz.
Āz opposes his extraction by reincorporating Light into generation and humanity.

Šilmai.note: Šilmai is invoked with Hibil and other light-beings in baptismal prayer.

Šitil.note: Šitil opens a drain with Hibil and makes heavenly spheres while Ptahil forms earth.

Šišlam Rabba.note: Adam Kasia is identified or closely coordinated with the primordial heavenly priest Šišlam.

Šišlam-Rba.note: Hibil and Šišlam-Rba jointly question their father Nbaṭ about esoteric teachings.
